title: Reconcile decision when-a-worktree-may-be-removed ("in every repo") with owner pick own-828-a ("this repo only" at session end)
why: Source: coordinator 20:19 CST Nov 14 (data, from lane #3438, the lane for own-828-a; triage read no code and no PR). Conflict as the lane states it: decision when-a-worktree-may-be-removed (stable clone 261bdceca, read by triage) says in its "Session-end sweep, agent rule" section, quoted: "Owner ruling, 2026-10-14: the session-end sweep (`sweep.py --confirm`, no `--attended`) removes a finished agent's worktree in every repo." Line 17 of its table says the same ("A finished agent's worktree at `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/agent-*`, in every repo"). Owner ruling own-828-a-sessionend-this-repo-only (page item 828 option a, 19:57:58 CST Nov 14): "This repo only at session end. Dead servers elsewhere wait for the daily job." The lane adds one note line and does not edit the decision. TRIAGE READ: own-828-a names DEAD SERVERS (janitor decision the-janitor-is-one-machine-wide-sweep, "Two triggers"), not worktree removal; the decision above names AGENT WORKTREES. So the two may be different acts and may not conflict at all; whether the lane's "own repo only" is meant to cover worktree removal too is UNKNOWN (the lane says it does; own-828-a's text does not say it). The lane's note line is not in the decision on the stable clone (261bdceca, 19:34 CST, before #3438): unread on the PR. Rule: git-one-record-per-question (rewrite the decision in place when its ruling changes; open no second record). Also: the simulator tier is left unchanged by the lane: an open reading, not asked. No owner question (the coordinator reads none as needed). 23:52 CST Nov 14 (triage; read of PR #3438 body by REST, merged 23:49:53 CST, and the janitor decision on main at merge commit 20963a214992): #3438 named this conflict and said triage routes it to the owner. Triage found a past owner ruling that answers it on its face: watchers-sessionend-250a (owner, page item 250 a, 2026-11-04; answer time not on record, so its date is the item's added date): "One repo at SessionEnd; machine-wide only in the daily job". The janitor decision "Two triggers" (on main) says: "A `SessionEnd` hook judges branches and worktrees only in the repository whose session ended (owner, Cockpit item 250 a, 2026-11-04 07:53 CST; coordinator reading, 09:47 CST)". The older decision when-a-worktree-may-be-removed (owner ruling 2026-10-14, line 69 on the stable clone, not re-read on main) says the session-end sweep "removes a finished agent's worktree in every repo" and its table line 17 says "in every repo". Newer owner ruling, narrower scope: so the older text is probably stale for the SessionEnd run. UNKNOWN: whether item 250 a was meant to narrow the 2026-10-14 agent-worktree rule (the item text says SessionEnd cleans one repo; it does not name agent worktrees). Fix by record rewrite, not owner item: git-one-record-per-question says rewrite when-a-worktree-may-be-removed in place so it states repo scope at SessionEnd (a lane edit for the coordinator). Posted no owner item: a filed owner ruling covers it; if the coordinator reads a real doubt that 250 a reached agent worktrees, that is the question to bring. Not read: the full text of #3438's diff and docs/debts/notes.md line naming both decisions.
note: Filed 20:22 CST Nov 14 by triage. First act of a lane: read the decision section "Session-end sweep, agent rule" and own-828-a option a text, and say whether they conflict for the SessionEnd act only, for worktree removal generally, or not at all (servers versus worktrees). If they conflict, rewrite the decision in place when the owner's ruling says so; if the owner's words do not cover worktrees, say so and ask nothing until the coordinator reads it as a question. Not started.
